supports: This 1,800-acre preserve protects sensitive marine habitats.
It includes one of the County's largest undeveloped barrier islands (Shell Key) as well as numerous mangrove islands and expansive seagrass beds.
Shell Key is one of the state's most important areas for shorebird nesting and wintering and serves as an important study area for these species.
No restroom facilities are provided.
Preserve is accessible only by boat.
Dogs and alcohol are not allowed anywhere in the preserve.
The closest boat ramps, trailer parking and restroom facilities are at Fort De Soto Park
Ferry Service from Fort De Soto Boat Ramp to Shell Key

editorial.hook: An undeveloped barrier island, a key shorebird nesting and wintering area, reached only by boat.

editorial.know_before: Boat access only, with a ferry from the Fort De Soto boat ramp. No restrooms, and no dogs or alcohol anywhere in the preserve.
editorial.local_tip: The closest boat ramps, trailer parking and restrooms are at Fort De Soto Park, so plan your restroom stop before you launch.

supports: The Orange County Regional History Center, housed in a historic courthouse in the heart of downtown Orlando, offers four floors of exhibits exploring 14,000 years of Central Florida’s rich heritage.
As an affiliate of the Smithsonian Institution, the History Center presents limited-run exhibitions of great depth and insight.
Convenient parking options include the Central Boulevard garage across from the Orlando Public Library, the History Center’s neighbor.
Mon-Sat: 10am - 5pm Sun: 12pm - 5pm

supports: Juan More’ established La Segunda Central Bakery in 1915.
One of our most important time-honored customs is placing a freshly cut palmetto leaf across the top of each loaf to create the signature split down the middle.
Each loaf is individually hand-placed into the hearth and left to bake for 45 minutes.
La Segunda is one of the very few bakeries to uphold this labor intensive tradition.
locals stopping in for their daily café con leche and Cuban toast
La Segunda Central Bakery from his partners, which stands today as one of Ybor’s coveted landmark buildings representing the Cuban-American era.
Skip the line and get your La Segunda favorites fast with online ordering.
La Segunda Bakery, 2512 North 15th Street, Tampa, FL, 33605

editorial.hook: Cuban bread baked since 1915 in an Ybor landmark, every loaf split by a fresh palmetto leaf.

editorial.know_before: Online ordering lets you skip the line.
editorial.local_tip: Stop in the way locals do, for a daily café con leche and Cuban toast.

evidence.source_name: Visit St. Augustine - Auggie's Draft Room (tourism DMO)
supports: St. Augustine's only self-serve tap house, Auggie's Draft Room has 24 beer taps offering a changing menu of well-known international brands such as Guinness and Corona to domestic beers and local craft brews as well.

Unlike other tap rooms, at Auggie's Draft Room, you exchange your credit card for a special draft room card that records all the beer you drink every time it's inserted into an empty slot above a tap.
Before you leave, exchange your draft card for your credit card and pay your bill.
For those who come with their friends, but don't have a taste for beer, there are ciders and a selection of wines.
Auggie's kitchen serves hot and cold sandwiches, fries, shrimp, wings, and salads.
Auggie's is open for breakfast on Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays, from 8:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m.
3 St. George Street

editorial.hook: St. Augustine's only self-serve tap house: 24 taps and a draft card that logs every pour.

supports: The name Homecomin' Florida Kitchen is a nod to Chef Art’s return to Walt Disney World after his first cast role in The Magic Kingdom College Program in 1981 – now known as the Walt Disney World College Program.
We’re serving Southern favorites such as Chef Art's signature fried chicken, shrimp and grits and our legendary Shine Cake.
So come over, sip a handcrafted moonshine cocktail on our back porch and enjoy the bubbling springs backdrop.
When you browse our menu, know that ingredients are Florida farm sourced and served at the peak of freshness, changing here and there with the seasons.
Special discounts are available to Cast Members and First Responders / Military. Ask your server for details.

supports: Encounter hundreds of authentic artifacts recovered from the ocean floor.
Stand in awe of Little Piece, a 2-ton section of Titanic ’s hull—the second-largest artifact ever recovered.
Feel the freezing temperatures of the Atlantic as you touch an iceberg chilled to match the water on the night Titanic sank.
Imagine life on the Ship as you walk through full-scale re-creations of iconic spaces like the Grand Staircase, First Class Suite, and Promenade Deck.
Guided tours are offered daily and led by costumed storytellers who share little-known details and personal accounts from Titanic ’s passengers and crew.
Most visitors spend 1.5 to 2 hours exploring the Exhibition, though you’re welcome to go at your own pace.

supports: It houses over 40 historic rail cars including Presidential Rail Car 'Ferdinand Magellan,' and Florida East Coast Steam Locomotive #153.
Founded in 1957, GCRM was built on the former Naval Air Station Richmond (NASR), the second largest WWII airship base in the United States.
The Gold Coast Railroad Museum became one of the three official Florida State Railroad Museums in 1984.
Besides its rail cars, the museum includes a model railroad room, a Naval Air Station Richmond exhibit, Thomas play tables, and multiple displays of rail equipment.
